introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Food and Nutrition 2 (0540), ORDINARY LEVEL, June 2024. Duration: two and a half hours.**

Instructions to candidates: ANSWER ANY FOUR QUESTIONS.

You are reminded of the necessity of good English and orderly presentation of work. Tabulate wherever possible and use diagrams where appropriate.
incertitudes: Règle de choix : la page de garde imprime « ANSWER ANY FOUR QUESTIONS » (4 sur 6 questions imprimées), sans section et sans mention « only the first four will be marked ». `groupes` = ["PAPER 2"] et `regles_choix` = parmi 4 sur 6, identiques dans les 6 fichiers.

Sujet scanné (CamScanner) de 2 pages : page de garde et six questions sur une page ; lu en image, aucun schéma ni figure imprimé, donc `figures` vide dans tous les fichiers. Filigranes (gcerevision.com, Kawlo) ignorés. L'en-tête imprimé « Food &Nutrition 2 » est recopié en « Food and Nutrition 2 » dans l'introduction ; les petites fautes de frappe du sujet (« five(5) », « Bring out five (5) importance of  food and nutrition », « types of food service  . ») sont recopiées telles quelles.

Points : chaque question imprime « Total = (25 marks) » et les points imprimés des sous-questions totalisent bien 25 pour les six questions (Q1 : 3+5+6+6+5 ; Q2 : 4+6+10+5 ; Q3 : 10+5+5+5 ; Q4 : 4+6+2+3+5+5 ; Q5 : 2+7+4+6+6 ; Q6 : 5+5+5+5+5) : aucun écart. Les sous-parties (i), (ii) restent dans le texte de la sous-question (d), 4(c), 4(d), 5(a) ou 6(d), dont `points` est la somme imprimée.

Aucun corrigé officiel : les corrigés sont des réponses modèles rédigées, au nombre exact d'éléments demandé, avec quelques réponses acceptables supplémentaires entre parenthèses. Aucune composition chiffrée de plat ou d'aliment n'est avancée ; les seuls chiffres sont les valeurs énergétiques classiques de la question 3(b), recalculées avec Python.

Question 3(b) : le sujet ne précise pas l'unité du résultat. Le corrigé donne 12 200 kJ par jour avec 17 kJ/g (glucides, protéines) et 37 kJ/g (lipides), et vérifie en kilocalories (2 900 kcal avec 4, 9 et 4 kcal/g) ; les deux résultats ont été recalculés avec Python. Un correcteur qui n'accepterait que les kilocalories ou une autre valeur par gramme (par exemple 16 kJ/g ou 4,2 kJ par kcal) trouverait un total voisin mais non identique.

Question 3(a) : la classification des légumes suit la partie consommée (feuilles, racines et tubercules, bulbes, fruits, graines et gousses) ; la tomate, botaniquement un fruit, est classée avec les légumes-fruits comme dans la plupart des manuels.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Classify five(5) vegetables stating an example each .

(10 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Vegetables are classified according to the **part of the plant** that is eaten. Five groups (1 mark for the class and 1 mark for the example):

| Class of vegetable | Part of the plant eaten | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **Leaves (leafy vegetables)** | the leaves | cabbage, lettuce or spinach |
| **Roots and tubers** | the root or the underground tuber | carrot, beetroot, Irish potato or yam |
| **Bulbs** | the swollen underground leaf bases | onion or garlic |
| **Fruits** | the fruit of the plant | tomato, cucumber, okra or green pepper |
| **Seeds and pods (legumes)** | the seeds, with or without the pod | green peas, beans or sweetcorn |

(Other correct classes: stems, for example celery or asparagus; flowers, for example cauliflower or broccoli.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
A diet contains 400g of carbohydrate, 100g of fat and 100g of protein. Calculate the energy value per day

(5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Energy values used:** 1 g of carbohydrate gives about 17 kJ, 1 g of protein gives about 17 kJ and 1 g of fat gives about 37 kJ.

| Nutrient | Mass | Energy per gram | Energy supplied |
|---|---|---|---|
| Carbohydrate | 400 g | 17 kJ | $400 \times 17 = 6\,800$ kJ |
| Fat | 100 g | 37 kJ | $100 \times 37 = 3\,700$ kJ |
| Protein | 100 g | 17 kJ | $100 \times 17 = 1\,700$ kJ |

**Total energy value per day**

$$6\,800 + 3\,700 + 1\,700 = 12\,200 \text{ kJ}$$

**The energy value of the diet is 12 200 kJ per day (12.2 MJ).**

Check in kilocalories, using 4 kcal per gram of carbohydrate and of protein and 9 kcal per gram of fat: $400 \times 4 + 100 \times 9 + 100 \times 4 = 1\,600 + 900 + 400 = 2\,900$ kcal per day.
themes: energy value of food and energy needs

questions.enonce_markdown:
List five (5) points to consider when choosing a refrigerator.

(5marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Five points to consider when choosing a refrigerator (1 mark each):

1. **The size (capacity)**, chosen according to the number of people in the family and the quantity of food to be stored.
2. **The price and the running cost.** The buyer must be able to afford the refrigerator and the cost of the electricity (or gas or kerosene) it uses; an energy-saving model costs less to run.
3. **The type and the source of energy.** An electric refrigerator needs a regular supply of electricity; where there is none, a gas, kerosene or solar model may be needed.
4. **The space available and the position.** It must fit the space in the kitchen, with room around it for the air to circulate, away from the cooker and from direct sunlight.
5. **The inside fittings and the quality.** Adjustable shelves, a freezer compartment, a vegetable drawer, a tight door seal, easy defrosting, easy cleaning, a guarantee and the maker's after-sales service.

questions.enonce_markdown:
State five (5) rules for food hygiene.

(5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Five rules for food hygiene (1 mark each):

1. **Wash the hands with soap and clean water before handling food, after using the toilet and after touching raw meat, fish or waste.**
2. **Keep the body and the clothes clean.** Wear a clean apron, tie up or cover the hair, keep the nails short and clean, and cover cuts and sores with a waterproof dressing.
3. **Keep the kitchen, the utensils and the work surfaces clean.** Wash them in hot soapy water and keep the rubbish in a covered bin.
4. **Wash fruit and vegetables well, cook food thoroughly and keep raw and cooked food apart** (use separate boards and knives for raw meat).
5. **Store food properly and protect it from flies and pests.** Keep perishable food cold or well covered, and eat cooked food soon or reheat it until it is very hot.
